newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets new rules to curb use of farmland.
newsitem.headline: China sets new rules to curb use of farmland.

text.p: China has ordered new rules governing the use of farmland in a bid to slow the loss of land to real estate development and stop speculation, the official Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.

It said the regulations, issued by the State Council (cabinet), would take effect immediately and require all provinces, autonomous regions and cities to prevent the amount of farmland from shrinking.
"The total acreage for cultivation can only increase and cannot be reduced," the regulations said. "The quality of land reserved for farming must also be improved."
Xinhua also said that some localities had arbitrarily used land without proper approval procedures.
"This has not only seriously affected agricultural development and the production of grain but has also affected the overall economy as well as social stability," the news agency said.
All local governments must report to central authorities on real estate development conducted since 1991. Reports had to be completed by the end of October.
China's central government would tighten approval procedures and bar the designation of any agricultural land for development over the next year.

As part of its effort to preserve land, it put an immediate freeze on the upgrading of any county to city status. City level status would give a local government more autonomy in many areas, including land development.
The amount of land set aside for development by cities would also be tightly controlled, it said.
State land could not be sold for redevelopment for construction of golf courses, amusement parks, luxury villas, temples or churches.
Other measures called for collectives not to sell land, except to the state.
All land linked to national security, the armed forces or part of priority areas of protection had to be approved by central authorities before it could be sold to foreigners.
The rules forbid the sale of any island in its entirety to foreign investors.
